key_insight: This paper explores whether self-distillation can work without any privileged answers or extra visual evidence, relying only on input conditioning to create a useful learning gap between teacher and student. The main takeaway is a simpler form of on-policy self-distillation that removes the need for asymmetric side information.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge in on-policy self-distillation of needing a stronger self-teacher than student, which existing methods typically achieve using privileged answers or additional visual evidence.
method: Construct an on-policy self-distillation setup where the teacher and student are derived from the same model and data stream.
Remove external teachers and eliminate asymmetric supervision sources such as privileged answers or extra visual cues.
Use input conditioning alone to induce the teacher-student asymmetry needed for effective learning.
impact: This matters because it simplifies self-distillation pipelines, reducing dependence on extra annotations or modalities. For practitioners, it can make training more flexible, cheaper, and easier to apply in settings where privileged information is unavailable.
